pois.name: Museum of Glass
pois.intro: The Museum of Glass is a 75,000-square-foot contemporary art museum in Tacoma, Washington, dedicated to the medium of glass. Since its founding in 2002, the Museum of Glass has been committed to creating a space for the celebration of the studio glass movement through nurturing artists, implementing education, and encouraging creativity.

pois.name: Browns Point Lighthouse
pois.intro: The Browns Point Lighthouse is a lighthouse located near Tacoma on Browns Point at the east entrance to Puget Sound's Commencement Bay, Pierce County, Washington.

pois.name: Wright Park
pois.intro: Wright Park is a 27-acre arboretum and public park located in Tacoma, Washington, that is managed by Metro Parks Tacoma. The park was designed by Bavarian landscape architect Edward Otto Schwagerl.

pois.name: The Fish Peddler on Foss Waterway
Tacoma Art Museum
pois.intro: The Tacoma Art Museum is an art museum in Tacoma, Washington, United States. It focuses primarily on the art and artists from the Pacific Northwest and broader western region of the U.S. Founded in 1935, the museum has strong roots in the community and anchors the university and museum district in downtown Tacoma.

pois.name: LeMay - America's Car Museum
pois.intro: LeMay - America's Car Museum is an automotive museum in the city of Tacoma, Washington, United States. Many of the cars on display were donated to the museum by the family of Harold LeMay.

pois.name: Point Defiance Zoo & Aquarium
pois.intro: Point Defiance Zoo & Aquarium is located in Tacoma, Washington, US, and is the only combined zoo and aquarium in the Pacific Northwest. PDZA is owned by Metro Parks Tacoma.

pois.name: Washington State History Museum
pois.intro: The Washington State History Museum is a history museum located in downtown Tacoma, Washington, United States. It is operated by the Washington State Historical Society under the official approval of the Washington State Legislature.

pois.name: USCGC Comanche
pois.intro: The second USS Wampanoag, originally USS ATA-202, is a United States Navy auxiliary ocean-going tug in commission from 1945 to 1947. USS ATA-202 was laid down on 24 August 1944 at Port Arthur, Texas, by the Gulfport Boiler and Welding Works.

pois.name: Children's Museum of Tacoma
pois.intro: Children's Museum of Tacoma is a nonprofit museum for children located in Tacoma, Washington. The museum officially opened in 1986.

pois.name: Working Waterfront Maritime Museum
pois.intro: The Working Waterfront Maritime Museum is a Maritime Museum located in Tacoma, Washington, USA. The museum sits on the Thea Foss Waterway. Along with the Discovery Wharf Children's Activity Area, the WWMM is a part of the Foss Waterway Seaport, a 501c3 non-profit organization founded in 1996.

pois.name: Wild Waves Theme Park
pois.address: 36201 Enchanted Parkway South, Federal Way, WA, 98003
pois.intro: Wild Waves Theme & Water Park was an amusement park and water park in Federal Way, Washington. Opened in 1977 as The Enchanted Village, the park is a popular summer destination in the Pacific Northwest.

pois.name: Fireboat No. 1
pois.intro: Fireboat No. 1 is a historic fireboat on display in a permanent land installation on the waterfront in the Old Town area of Tacoma, Washington.

pois.name: USCGC Tiger
pois.intro: The USCGC Tiger was an Active-class patrol boat of the United States Coast Guard.

pois.name: Fort Nisqually
pois.intro: Fort Nisqually was an important fur trading and farming post of the Hudson's Bay Company in the Puget Sound area, part of the Hudson's Bay Company's Columbia Department. It was located in what is now DuPont, Washington.

pois.name: Old City Hall Historic District
pois.intro: The Old City Hall Historic District is located on a bluff at the north end of Tacoma's business district, overlooking Commencement Bay. The Old City Hall and the Northern Pacific Office Building stabilize the northern boundary of the district and the Pantages Theatre/Jones Building just south of the district boundary, complements the Winthrop Hotel.

pois.name: North 21st Street
pois.intro: The North 21st Street Bridge in Tacoma, Washington was built in 1910. It was designed by engineers Waddell & Harrington and is a continuous concrete rigid-frame girder bridge.

pois.name: Manifesto Coffee Roasters
pois.description: Our high-quality coffee beans are carefully sourced and roasted to perfection. We have a simplified menu that caters to all tastes, and our friendly and knowledgeable staff is always on hand to suggest the perfect pastry to complement your drink.

pois.name: The Commons At Federal Way
pois.address: 1928 South Commons, Federal Way, WA, 98003, US
pois.intro: The Commons at Federal Way is a regional shopping mall located in Federal Way, Washington, and is the only indoor shopping center in the city. Steadfast Commercial Properties changed the mall's name to The Commons at Federal Way in November 2003 as part of a redevelopment program.

pois.name: Dash Point State Park
pois.intro: Dash Point State Park is a 398-acre Washington public recreation area on Puget Sound that straddles the line between King and Pierce counties. The state park has over 3,300 feet of shoreline, 140 campsites, 11 miles of trails for hiking and mountain biking, and offers beachcombing, fishing, swimming, birdwatching, windsurfing, skimboarding, and wildlife viewing.
